Translingual

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Abbreviation of English Seim.

Symbol

[edit]

sim

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Mende (New Guinea).

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Mende (New Guinea) terms

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sɪm/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɪm

Noun

[edit]

sim (plural sims)

  2. (informal) Clipping of simulator.
    They played a flight sim all afternoon.
    • 2009 July 11, Darren Zenko, “U.K. pair turn time into romp”, in Toronto Star‎[1]:
      But shooters, sims and real-time strategy games ascended as the industry grew and mouseless home consoles made the genre's mechanics awkward.
  4. (informal) Clipping of simulation.
  5. (informal) A simulation session or scenario.
    (Can we add an example for this sense?)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • city sim
  • dating sim
  • dim sim
  • farming sim
  • farm sim
  • life sim
  • management sim
  • racesim
  • raising sim
  • sim-com
  • simmer
  • simrace
  • sim racer
  • simworld
  • walking sim

See also

[edit]
  • emulator
  • model
  • trainer

Verb

[edit]

sim (third-person singular simple present sims, present participle simming, simple past and past participle simmed)

  2. (informal, uncommon) Clipping of simulate.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • -ism, IMS, IMs, ISM, MIS, MIs, MSI, ism, mis-

Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • si, sí (dialectal)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese si (“yes”) (with nasalization of the vowel under the influence of não or mim), from Latin sīc (“thus; so”), from Proto-Indo-European *so (“this, that”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈsĩ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈsĩ/

  • Rhymes: -ĩ
  • Hyphenation: sim
  • Audio (Brazil):(file)
  • Audio (Brazil (São Paulo)):(file)
  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)

Interjection

[edit]

sim

  1. yes (affirmative answer)
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:sim
    Antonyms: não; see also Thesaurus:sim
    “Eles já saíram?” “Sim, saíram.”
    “Have they left?” “Yes, they have.”

Usage notes

[edit]

Sim as an affirmative response is relatively uncommon in Portuguese. The typical affirmative response in the language consists of repeating the first verb of the question, with a change in person if necessary:

  • “Eles saíram?” “Saíram.”
    “Have they left?” “Yes.”
  • “Eu ganhei?” “ganhaste/ ganhou.”
    “Have I won?” “You have.”
  • “Você vai sair?” “vou.”
    “Are you going out?” “I am.”

Derived terms

[edit]
  • porque sim

Adverb

[edit]

sim (not comparable)

  1. indeed; do (used for emphasis in affirmative expressions)
    Eu já li esse livro sim.
    I have already read this book indeed.
    Ele matou sim o bicho.
    He did kill the bug.

Noun

[edit]

sim m (plural sins)

  1. yes; yea (an affirmative answer)
    Antonym: não
    Recebemos um sim e três nãos.
    We got one yes and three noes.

  • “sim”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
